buildConfig.intro: Configure the build environment for FFmpeg. The build shell and build tools are installed inside the workspace folder.

buildConfig.technical.title: Details
buildConfig.technical.shell.ucrt64.title: ucrt64 (recommended)
buildConfig.technical.shell.ucrt64.text: ucrt64 builds FFmpeg against the Universal C Runtime (UCRT), the modern C runtime that ships with Windows 10 and later. It is the recommended default because it produces modern binaries that match current Windows and is the best-supported MSYS2 environment. (Choose this option unless you need compatibility with older devices.)
buildConfig.technical.shell.mingw64.text: mingw64 uses the traditional MinGW-w64 toolchain and builds against the older MSVCRT runtime instead of UCRT. (Choose it only when you need compatibility with older Windows versions or tooling that expects MSVCRT; it is rarely needed for modern builds.)
buildConfig.technical.shell.clang64.text: clang64 builds with the LLVM/Clang compiler instead of GCC. (Choose it only when you need Clang-specific behavior or diagnostics, or compatibility with dependencies also built with Clang; it is not needed for a standard FFmpeg build.)
buildConfig.technical.packages.title: Package list
buildConfig.technical.packages.text: Each line is one package installed by the private package manager (MSYS2 pacman). The program installs these packages into the workspace copy of MSYS2.
buildConfig.technical.scope.title: What belongs here
buildConfig.technical.scope.text: This list is only for build tools such as compilers, make, pkg-config, CMake, Ninja, NASM, and YASM. Codec libraries are selected in the FFmpeg Libraries tab.
buildConfig.technical.tools.title: What each build tool does
buildConfig.technical.tool.base-devel: Meta-package of core Unix build utilities (shell, coreutils, sed, grep, and more) that build scripts rely on.
buildConfig.technical.tool.git: Version-control tool used to fetch source code from repositories.
buildConfig.technical.tool.make: GNU Make — runs Makefiles to drive compilation and linking.
buildConfig.technical.tool.diffutils: Provides diff and related tools, used by configure scripts and patching.
buildConfig.technical.tool.binutils: Assembler, linker, and binary tools (as, ld, objdump) for the target platform.
buildConfig.technical.tool.crt: MinGW-w64 C runtime startup files the compiler links into every binary.
buildConfig.technical.tool.gcc: The GNU C/C++ compiler that builds FFmpeg's source code.
buildConfig.technical.tool.headers: MinGW-w64 Windows API headers the compiler needs to target Windows.
buildConfig.technical.tool.libmangle: Helper library the MinGW-w64 toolchain uses internally for symbol name handling.
buildConfig.technical.tool.libwinpthread: Runtime import library for winpthreads, providing POSIX threads on Windows.
buildConfig.technical.tool.pkgconf: pkg-config implementation that reports compiler and linker flags for installed libraries.
buildConfig.technical.tool.tools: Extra MinGW-w64 utilities (gendef, widl, and others) used when building Windows code.
buildConfig.technical.tool.winpthreads: POSIX threads (pthreads) implementation for Windows, required by threaded code.
buildConfig.technical.tool.winstorecompa: Compatibility shims that let modern builds run against older Windows API versions.
buildConfig.technical.tool.cmake: Cross-platform build-system generator used by some libraries.
buildConfig.technical.tool.ninja: Fast build backend that CMake can drive instead of Make.
buildConfig.technical.tool.nasm: x86/x86-64 assembler used to build hand-written SIMD assembly.
buildConfig.technical.tool.yasm: Alternative x86 assembler some components use for SIMD assembly.

libraries.row.unavailable.tensorflow: Temporarily unavailable: as of this program's development, FFmpeg's own TensorFlow DNN backend does not compile in any FFmpeg official source release up to the latest (8.x), so enabling it would break the build. The download/import support is kept and will be re-enabled once a fixed official FFmpeg release is available.

It will be re-enabled once an official FFmpeg release includes it.
libraries.presets.minimal.name: Minimal
libraries.presets.minimal.plain: Plain FFmpeg source build with only default programs and core libraries.
libraries.presets.minimal.technical: (As of FFmpeg 8.1.2) No external codec or multimedia package is added. This is what you get from a plain FFmpeg source compile without extra --enable-lib flags.
libraries.presets.default.name: Default
libraries.presets.default.plain: Common Windows-style build for hardware encoding, codecs, subtitles, and protocols.
libraries.presets.default.technical: (As of FFmpeg 8.1.2) Includes hardware encoders (NVENC, AMF, QSV), major video codecs (H.264, H.265, VP9, AV1, Theora, Xvid), common audio codecs, subtitle rendering, stabilization, and standard protocol support. Closely follows the gyan.dev release-essentials build profile, with fast AV1 encode/decode (SVT-AV1, dav1d) added.
libraries.presets.efficiency.name: Maximum Efficiency
libraries.presets.efficiency.plain: Quality-focused set with stronger AAC encoding, cleaner resampling, and a better AV1 encoder.
libraries.presets.efficiency.technical: (As of FFmpeg 8.1.2) Includes everything in Default plus FDK AAC (best AAC encoder), the SoX high-quality resampler, and the rav1e quality-focused AV1 encoder. In Extended mode it also adds vvenc (VVC/H.266) and LCEVC enhancement decoding. The preset follows feature goals first; the derived license boundary is shown later in Build FFmpeg.
libraries.presets.compatibility.name: Maximum Compatibility
libraries.presets.compatibility.plain: Wider media-format set with more codecs, captions, images, and streaming input.
libraries.presets.compatibility.technica: (As of FFmpeg 8.1.2) Includes everything in Default plus the OpenH264 encoder, EVC encode/decode (xeve/xevd), APV (oapv) and AVS1 (xavs) encoding, iLBC, TwoLAME, Codec 2 and LC3 speech, the Shine MP3 encoder, Snappy for HAP, SVG input, teletext and ARIB caption decoding, and RTMP streaming. In Extended mode it also adds AVS2/AVS3 decoding (davs2/uavs3d), AVS2 encoding (xavs2), AviSynth+ input, and broadcast metadata (klvanc). Stays a free-license set (no nonfree libraries). The preset follows compatibility first; the derived license boundary is shown later in Build FFmpeg.
libraries.presets.editor.name: Audio/Video Editor
libraries.presets.editor.plain: Editing-focused set with filters, color, subtitles, plugins, analysis, and transcription.
libraries.presets.editor.technical: (As of FFmpeg 8.1.2) Includes everything in Default plus PNG and JPEG XL images, lcms2 color management, libplacebo GPU processing with Vulkan shader compilation (shaderc), frei0r effects, OpenCV and OpenColorIO, XML parsing, SOFA (mysofa) and bs2b binaural audio, LADSPA and LV2 audio plugin hosting, Chromaprint fingerprinting, QR generation, and whisper speech-to-text. In Extended mode it also adds AviSynth+ input, LCEVC enhancement decoding, and QR decoding (quirc). Stays a free-license set (no nonfree libraries). The preset follows editor usefulness first; the derived license boundary is shown later in Build FFmpeg.
libraries.presets.full.name: Full
libraries.presets.full.plain: Broadest safe set with discs, devices, networks, OCR, and special outputs.
libraries.presets.full.technical: (As of FFmpeg 8.1.2) The broadest conflict-free set: the union of Efficiency, Compatibility, and Editor plus Kvazaar (HEVC), Blu-ray/DVD/CD input, module audio, OpenGL output, OpenSSL TLS, RIST/RabbitMQ streaming or messaging, Tesseract OCR, JACK/PulseAudio, OpenCL GPU acceleration, and libcaca output. In Extended mode it also adds vvenc, AVS2/AVS3, AviSynth+, MPEG-H decoding, QR decoding (quirc), and broadcast metadata (klvanc). GnuTLS is left unchecked because FFmpeg cannot enable GnuTLS and OpenSSL at the same time, and glslang is left to shaderc for the same reason.

source.msys2.technical.intro: MSYS2 is a Unix-like build environment for Windows. It provides the shell, compilers (GCC), and package manager that FFmpeg's build expects. FFmpeg is built with Unix-style tools that Windows does not include, so MSYS2 supplies that exact toolchain. This program installs a private MSYS2 inside the workspace and uses it to fetch packages and then configure, compile, and link FFmpeg, all kept within the workspace.
source.msys2.technical.archive.title: Archive requirements
source.msys2.technical.archive.text: Use a portable MSYS2 archive. .tar.zst is recommended, but .tar.xz also works. (.exe or .sfx.exe files may be the official MSYS2 installer or self-extracting files, but this program does not use that format.)
source.msys2.technical.sha.text: Entering the verification checksum (SHA-256) is optional. If you do not provide it, the program calculates the SHA-256 after the MSYS2 download and logs it. (Use the digital signature for verification; use the checksum only as an extra verification value when you already have a trusted hash.)
source.ffmpeg.technical.archive.title: Archive requirements
source.ffmpeg.technical.archive.text: Use an official FFmpeg source archive such as "ffmpeg-8.1.tar.xz". (Use a source code archive, not a prebuilt Windows executable package.)
source.ffmpeg.technical.sha.text: Entering the verification checksum (SHA-256) is optional. If you do not provide it, the program calculates the SHA-256 after the FFmpeg source download and logs it. (Use the digital signature for verification; use the checksum only as an extra verification value when you already have a trusted hash.)
source.msys2Signature.hint: Enter the location of the .sig file that matches the archive's digital signature. The program downloads that signature and then verifies the archive. (You do not need to install GPG yourself, and do not paste the contents of the .sig file into the field below.)
source.ffmpegSignature.hint: Enter the location of the .asc file, the digital signature that matches the source code archive. (Do not paste the PGP signature text into this field.)
catalog.libraries.libmfx.plainExplanatio: Legacy Intel hardware encoding and decoding through the older Media SDK. Mainly for older setups; on newer ones, the oneVPL option above is the better choice.
catalog.libraries.libmfx.technicalExplan: The Media SDK dispatcher loads Intel's fixed-function media runtime at run time instead of linking it directly, so the build only needs the dispatcher. No prebuilt package ships it, so this builder compiles Intel's open mfx_dispatch from source. It cannot be enabled alongside the newer oneVPL backend - FFmpeg's configure rejects having both.
catalog.libraries.amf.plainExplanation: Provides AMD GPU video encoding for faster H.264, HEVC, and AV1 output on supported Radeon systems. Useful when speed and low CPU use matter.
catalog.libraries.amf.technicalExplanati: AMF uses AMD’s hardware media engine rather than pure CPU encoding. It is best suited for real-time conversion, recording, and streaming where throughput is more important than the deepest software-side compression search.
catalog.libraries.aom.plainExplanation: Supports AV1 encoding through the reference AV1 codec family. Strong quality and standards-oriented behavior, usually chosen when output quality matters more than encoding speed.
catalog.libraries.aom.technicalExplanati: AOM focuses on AV1’s full coding toolset, including complex prediction and rate-distortion decisions. It can produce efficient AV1 streams, but its deeper analysis makes encoding slower than speed-oriented AV1 encoders.
catalog.libraries.aribb24.plainExplanati: Handles ARIB B24 captions used in Japanese broadcast material. Useful for preserving or processing older broadcast subtitle data.
catalog.libraries.aribb24.technicalExpla: ARIB B24 is a bitmap- and control-code-based caption system used in ISDB broadcasting. This library helps interpret those caption streams so they can be decoded, converted, or carried through media workflows.
catalog.libraries.aribcaption.plainExpla: Reads Japanese broadcast captions with better modern ARIB caption handling. Useful for TV recordings and broadcast transport streams.
catalog.libraries.aribcaption.technicalE: ARIB caption streams contain timed text, layout, styling, and broadcast-specific character handling. This library focuses on decoding that caption data into usable subtitle information.
catalog.libraries.ass.plainExplanation: Renders advanced ASS/SSA subtitles with fonts, colors, placement, outlines, and animation-like effects. Commonly used for complex subtitle presentation.
catalog.libraries.ass.technicalExplanati: libass performs text shaping, styling, positioning, karaoke effects, borders, shadows, and font-based subtitle rendering. It is important when subtitles must be burned into video exactly as designed.
catalog.libraries.bluray.plainExplanatio: Reads Blu-ray disc structures for inspection, conversion, or extraction workflows. Useful when the source is organized as Blu-ray folders rather than a single media file.
catalog.libraries.bluray.technicalExplan: Blu-ray input involves playlists, clips, stream selection, chapters, and disc metadata. libbluray helps interpret that structure so the intended program stream can be accessed correctly.
catalog.libraries.bs2b.plainExplanation: Applies headphone crossfeed to make stereo listening feel less hard-panned and more speaker-like. Useful for headphone-focused audio processing.
catalog.libraries.bs2b.technicalExplanat: Crossfeed mixes a controlled amount of each stereo channel into the other with delay and filtering. This reduces extreme left-right separation and can make long headphone listening more natural.
catalog.libraries.opengl.plainExplanatio: Adds the OpenGL output device for hardware-accelerated video display through OpenGL. Provided by the Mesa package.
catalog.libraries.opengl.technicalExplan: --enable-opengl builds FFmpeg's OpenGL rendering output device. The Mesa package supplies the GL headers; on Windows the device links the system opengl32 and gdi32 libraries. Useful mainly for display/playback paths rather than file output.
catalog.libraries.dc1394.plainExplanatio: Captures video from IEEE 1394 (FireWire) cameras. Blocked on Windows: no MSYS2 package, and the only Windows build needs a proprietary FireWire kernel driver plus FireWire hardware, so the result would not be portable.
catalog.libraries.dc1394.technicalExplan: libdc1394 implements the IIDC/DCAM protocol over IEEE 1394 (FireWire), exposing machine-vision cameras as a raw capture source. Mainline libdc1394 has no Windows transport backend — only Linux (raw1394/juju) and macOS. The one Windows port (indigo-astronomy fork) needs the proprietary CMU 1394Camera SDK at build time and a CMU kernel driver that replaces the native Windows FireWire driver at runtime. Even if built it requires physical FireWire hardware, so it cannot produce a portable static binary. Same redistribution and portability class as decklink.
catalog.libraries.decklink.plainExplanat: Adds Blackmagic DeckLink capture and playback support. It builds against the proprietary DeckLink SDK headers, which cannot be redistributed as an MSYS2 package.
catalog.libraries.decklink.technicalExpl: DeckLink is Blackmagic's line of professional SDI/HDMI capture and playback cards. FFmpeg drives them through Blackmagic's DeckLinkAPI SDK (headers version 10.6.1 or newer), providing uncompressed video and audio I/O for broadcast and live-production workflows.
catalog.libraries.caca.plainExplanation: Converts video into colored text-mode visuals. Mostly useful for experiments, terminal display, and unusual preview effects.
catalog.libraries.caca.technicalExplanat: libcaca maps image brightness and color into character cells. The result is not normal video compression, but a stylized text representation of moving images.
catalog.libraries.cdio.plainExplanation: Reads disc-based CD input for audio extraction and media inspection workflows. Useful when the source is an actual CD rather than copied audio files.
catalog.libraries.cdio.technicalExplanat: libcdio works with CD tracks, sectors, and disc metadata. It helps access audio or data from the disc layout instead of treating the source as an ordinary file.
catalog.libraries.chromaprint.plainExpla: Generates compact audio fingerprints for track matching and identification. Useful for recognizing audio even when filenames or metadata are missing.
catalog.libraries.chromaprint.technicalE: Chromaprint analyzes perceptual audio features and converts them into a fingerprint. The fingerprint can be compared against databases or other fingerprints to identify matching recordings.
catalog.libraries.codec2.plainExplanatio: Supports very low-bitrate speech coding for radio, voice, and communication experiments. Useful when intelligible speech must fit into extremely small bitrates.
catalog.libraries.codec2.technicalExplan: Codec 2 is designed for speech, not music. It models voice characteristics so spoken audio can remain understandable at bitrates far below general-purpose audio codecs.
catalog.libraries.dav1d.plainExplanation: Provides fast AV1 video decoding. Useful for smooth playback, inspection, and conversion of AV1 files.
catalog.libraries.dav1d.technicalExplana: dav1d is a highly optimized AV1 decoder focused on speed, threading, and CPU-specific acceleration. It is commonly used when AV1 decoding performance matters.
catalog.libraries.fdk-aac.plainExplanati: Produces high-quality AAC audio for MP4, mobile devices, streaming, and web playback. Often chosen when AAC quality is important.
catalog.libraries.fdk-aac.technicalExpla: Fraunhofer FDK AAC uses advanced AAC encoding modes and careful psychoacoustic modeling. It is especially valued for efficient audio quality at common music and speech bitrates.
catalog.libraries.ffmpeg-program.plainEx: The main command-line media processor for conversion, filtering, recording, streaming, and packaging.
catalog.libraries.ffmpeg-program.technic: This executable connects demuxing, decoding, filtering, encoding, and muxing into one command-driven workflow. It is the primary user-facing FFmpeg program.
catalog.libraries.ffprobe-program.plainE: Inspects media files and reports streams, codecs, metadata, chapters, durations, and technical structure.
catalog.libraries.ffprobe-program.techni: ffprobe reads containers and streams without performing a full conversion. It is useful for validation, automation, debugging, and checking what a media file actually contains.
catalog.libraries.fontconfig.plainExplan: Finds installed fonts so subtitle and text rendering can use the right typefaces. Useful for reliable text appearance.
catalog.libraries.fontconfig.technicalEx: Fontconfig matches font family names, styles, weights, and fallback fonts. It helps subtitle rendering avoid missing-font problems and incorrect replacements.
catalog.libraries.freetype.plainExplanat: Renders font glyphs for subtitles, overlays, and text-based filters. Essential when text must appear as real shaped graphics.
catalog.libraries.freetype.technicalExpl: FreeType rasterizes font outlines into pixels. It handles glyph metrics and rendering quality, making it central to clean subtitle and text drawing.
catalog.libraries.frei0r.plainExplanatio: Provides extra creative video effects and filter plugins. Useful for stylized processing beyond the standard filter set.
catalog.libraries.frei0r.technicalExplan: Frei0r is a plugin collection for video effects such as color manipulation, distortions, transitions, and generators. It expands the available visual filter vocabulary.
catalog.libraries.fribidi.plainExplanati: Handles right-to-left text direction for languages such as Arabic and Hebrew. Useful when subtitles or overlays contain bidirectional text.
catalog.libraries.fribidi.technicalExpla: FriBidi applies the Unicode bidirectional algorithm. It reorders mixed left-to-right and right-to-left text so visual rendering follows the intended reading order.
catalog.libraries.gme.plainExplanation: Reads classic game music formats from older consoles and systems. Useful for playback or conversion of chiptune-style sources.
catalog.libraries.gme.technicalExplanati: Game Music Emu emulates audio playback logic from legacy game systems. It turns compact game music data into decoded audio samples.
catalog.libraries.gnutls.plainExplanatio: Provides encrypted network connections for HTTPS and other TLS-based media access. Useful for secure streaming and remote sources.
catalog.libraries.gnutls.technicalExplan: GnuTLS handles certificate negotiation, encryption, and secure transport sessions. It protects media transfers that happen over TLS-based protocols.
catalog.libraries.gsm.plainExplanation: Handles legacy GSM speech audio. Useful for old voice recordings, telephony archives, and compatibility cases.
catalog.libraries.gsm.technicalExplanati: GSM audio is optimized for narrowband speech rather than general sound. The codec represents voice at low bitrate using speech-focused modeling.
catalog.libraries.harfbuzz.plainExplanat: Shapes complex text so letters combine, reorder, and position correctly. Important for subtitles in many non-Latin scripts.
catalog.libraries.harfbuzz.technicalExpl: HarfBuzz converts Unicode text into positioned glyphs. It handles ligatures, combining marks, contextual forms, and script-specific shaping rules.
catalog.libraries.ilbc.plainExplanation: Supports iLBC speech audio used in older internet voice communication. Useful for voice-call recordings and compatibility workflows.
catalog.libraries.ilbc.technicalExplanat: iLBC is designed for packet-based speech transmission. It preserves intelligibility under network loss better than general-purpose audio codecs of its era.
catalog.libraries.ladspa.plainExplanatio: Loads LADSPA audio effect plugins for extra audio processing. Useful when existing plugin chains need to be used in media conversion.
catalog.libraries.ladspa.technicalExplan: LADSPA plugins expose audio filters such as EQ, delay, compression, and synthesis-style effects. The host passes audio buffers through these plugin processors.
catalog.libraries.lc3.plainExplanation: Handles LC3 audio used in modern low-complexity communication audio. Useful for Bluetooth- and voice-oriented compatibility.
catalog.libraries.lc3.technicalExplanati: LC3 is designed for efficient speech and general audio at low delay and modest bitrate. It is associated with newer communication and wireless audio ecosystems.
catalog.libraries.lcms2.plainExplanation: Applies color profile management for more accurate color conversion. Useful when preserving color appearance matters.
catalog.libraries.lcms2.technicalExplana: Little CMS handles ICC profiles, color transforms, tone curves, and device-independent color conversion. It helps maintain intended color across different color spaces.
catalog.libraries.lensfun.plainExplanati: Corrects lens distortion, vignetting, and other camera-lens artifacts. Useful for cleanup of footage from known lenses.
catalog.libraries.lensfun.technicalExpla: lensfun uses camera and lens profiles to model optical behavior. It can compensate for barrel distortion, pincushion distortion, chromatic aberration, and darkened corners.
catalog.libraries.libavcodec.plainExplan: FFmpeg’s built-in codec library for decoding and encoding many media formats.
catalog.libraries.libavcodec.technicalEx: libavcodec contains the core codec implementations and wrappers used by FFmpeg. It turns compressed streams into frames and frames back into compressed streams.
catalog.libraries.libavfilter.plainExpla: FFmpeg’s built-in filtering library for video, audio, subtitles, scaling, overlays, and effects.
catalog.libraries.libavfilter.technicalE: libavfilter builds processing graphs where decoded frames pass through filters. It handles timing, format negotiation, and chained transformations.
catalog.libraries.libavformat.plainExpla: FFmpeg’s built-in container library for reading and writing formats such as MP4, MOV, MKV, WAV, and MPEG-TS.
catalog.libraries.libavformat.technicalE: libavformat separates container handling from codec handling. It reads packets from files or streams and writes encoded packets back into container structures.
catalog.libraries.libavutil.plainExplana: Shared FFmpeg utility code used across codecs, filters, formats, and tools.
catalog.libraries.libavutil.technicalExp: libavutil provides common data structures, math, pixel formats, sample formats, buffers, timestamps, and low-level helpers used throughout FFmpeg.
catalog.libraries.libjxl.plainExplanatio: Reads and writes JPEG XL images for modern high-quality still-image compression. Useful for image sequences and advanced image workflows.
catalog.libraries.libjxl.technicalExplan: JPEG XL supports lossless and lossy coding, wide color, high bit depth, animation, and efficient recompression of JPEG-like content.
catalog.libraries.libplacebo.plainExplan: Provides high-quality GPU video processing for scaling, color conversion, tone mapping, and rendering paths.
catalog.libraries.libplacebo.technicalEx: libplacebo is built around modern GPU rendering pipelines. It is known for precise color handling, HDR tone mapping, dithering, and advanced resampling algorithms.
catalog.libraries.libswresample.plainExp: Converts audio sample rates, sample formats, and channel layouts.
catalog.libraries.libswresample.technica: libswresample handles resampling, remixing, and sample-format conversion. It prepares audio so filters, encoders, and outputs receive compatible sample data.
catalog.libraries.libswscale.plainExplan: Converts image sizes and pixel formats.
catalog.libraries.libswscale.technicalEx: libswscale performs frame scaling and pixel-format conversion. It is a core compatibility layer between decoders, filters, encoders, and display/output formats.
catalog.libraries.libvpx.plainExplanatio: Produces VP8 and VP9 video, commonly used for WebM and web-oriented delivery.
catalog.libraries.libvpx.technicalExplan: libvpx performs block-based VPx encoding with rate control, temporal prediction, and web-focused codec tools. VP9 is especially useful for open web video compression.
catalog.libraries.lv2.plainExplanation: Loads LV2 audio plugins for more advanced audio effects and processing chains.
catalog.libraries.lv2.technicalExplanati: LV2 is a plugin standard for audio processors, instruments, and analysis tools. It supports richer plugin metadata and control models than older plugin systems.
catalog.libraries.modplug.plainExplanati: Reads old tracker module music formats. Useful for converting or playing legacy scene and game-style music files.
catalog.libraries.modplug.technicalExpla: Module files store patterns, samples, and playback instructions rather than a final waveform. libmodplug renders that sequenced data into audio.
catalog.libraries.mp3lame.plainExplanati: Produces MP3 audio with broad playback compatibility. Useful when the output must work on almost any device or player.
catalog.libraries.mp3lame.technicalExpla: LAME is a mature psychoacoustic MP3 encoder. It balances masking, bitrate allocation, stereo coding, and quantization to produce efficient MP3 output.
catalog.libraries.mysofa.plainExplanatio: Provides spatial audio filter data for headphone-based 3D audio rendering.
catalog.libraries.mysofa.technicalExplan: SOFA files store measured head-related impulse responses. libmysofa reads that data so audio can be filtered to simulate direction and space over headphones.
catalog.libraries.native-codecs.plainExp: Uses FFmpeg’s built-in codec support before adding external codec libraries.
catalog.libraries.native-codecs.technica: Native codecs are implemented inside FFmpeg itself. They cover many decoders and encoders without relying on external codec projects.
catalog.libraries.native-formats.plainEx: Uses FFmpeg’s built-in readers and writers for many media containers.
catalog.libraries.native-formats.technic: Native demuxers and muxers handle container structures, packet timing, stream metadata, and file layout for common media formats.
catalog.libraries.nvenc.plainExplanation: Provides NVIDIA GPU video encoding for fast H.264, HEVC, and AV1 output on supported NVIDIA systems.
catalog.libraries.nvenc.technicalExplana: NVENC uses NVIDIA’s dedicated hardware encoder. It is strong for real-time recording, streaming, and high-throughput conversion with low CPU load.
catalog.libraries.oapv.plainExplanation: Supports APV video encoding for specialized professional video workflows.
catalog.libraries.oapv.technicalExplanat: APV is designed around high-quality professional production use cases. The encoder targets intra/intermediate-style media needs rather than consumer playback ubiquity.
catalog.libraries.openal.plainExplanatio: Provides additional audio device input and output paths. Useful for workflows involving live audio devices.
catalog.libraries.openal.technicalExplan: OpenAL abstracts audio capture and playback devices. It is mainly relevant when media processing must interact with device-level audio streams.
catalog.libraries.opencl.plainExplanatio: Runs supported compute filters on OpenCL-capable GPUs or accelerators. Useful for offloading heavy image processing.
catalog.libraries.opencl.technicalExplan: OpenCL executes parallel kernels across GPU or accelerator hardware. In video processing, it can speed up operations that map well to many parallel pixels.
catalog.libraries.opencore-amr.plainExpl: Reads and writes AMR speech audio used by older mobile and voice systems.
catalog.libraries.opencore-amr.technical: AMR is optimized for narrowband and wideband speech. It models voice efficiently at low bitrates rather than preserving full-range music.
catalog.libraries.openh264.plainExplanat: Provides H.264 software encoding with a simpler encoder profile. Useful when basic H.264 output is needed without x264’s full decision depth.
catalog.libraries.openh264.technicalExpl: OpenH264 focuses on practical real-time H.264 encoding and decoding. Compared with x264, it generally offers fewer advanced compression controls and less exhaustive analysis.
catalog.libraries.openjpeg.plainExplanat: Reads and writes JPEG 2000 images used in archival, cinema, and professional imaging workflows.
catalog.libraries.openjpeg.technicalExpl: JPEG 2000 uses wavelet-based compression rather than block DCT-style compression. It supports high bit depth, lossless coding, and precise image preservation workflows.
catalog.libraries.openmpt.plainExplanati: Reads tracker module music with accurate playback behavior. Useful for old game, demo-scene, and tracker music formats.
catalog.libraries.openmpt.technicalExpla: OpenMPT renders pattern-based music formats into audio. It handles module-specific effects, instruments, tempo behavior, and playback quirks.
catalog.libraries.openssl.plainExplanati: Provides encrypted network connections for HTTPS and other secure media protocols.
catalog.libraries.openssl.technicalExpla: OpenSSL implements TLS, cryptography, certificate verification, and encrypted transport. It is widely used for secure network communication.
catalog.libraries.opus.plainExplanation: Produces modern Opus audio for speech, music, streaming, and low-latency communication.
catalog.libraries.opus.technicalExplanat: Opus combines speech-oriented and music-oriented coding modes. It adapts well across bitrates, handles low delay, and performs strongly for both voice and general audio.
catalog.libraries.png.plainExplanation: Handles PNG image input and output for lossless still images and image sequences.
catalog.libraries.png.technicalExplanati: PNG uses lossless compression with support for transparency and indexed or truecolor images. It is useful when exact image preservation matters.
catalog.libraries.qrencode.plainExplanat: Generates QR codes that can be placed into images or video frames.
catalog.libraries.qrencode.technicalExpl: QR encoding converts text or binary data into a two-dimensional barcode with error correction. The result can survive scaling, display capture, and partial damage.
catalog.libraries.libvpl.plainExplanatio: Provides Intel Quick Sync hardware encoding for fast video output with low CPU use, through the modern oneVPL runtime.
catalog.libraries.libvpl.technicalExplan: oneVPL (libvpl) is Intel's current media dispatcher, the successor to the legacy Media SDK (libmfx). It drives Intel’s dedicated media hardware for efficient real-time encoding, decoding, and processing on supported Intel systems. FFmpeg added oneVPL support in 6.0, so it is offered only on FFmpeg 6.0+; on older releases use libmfx instead. It cannot be enabled alongside libmfx.
catalog.libraries.rav1e.plainExplanation: Provides AV1 software encoding with a Rust-based encoder. Useful for comparing AV1 speed, quality, and encoder behavior.
catalog.libraries.rav1e.technicalExplana: rav1e emphasizes safe implementation and practical AV1 encoding. It uses AV1 prediction and transform tools with speed levels that control analysis depth.
catalog.libraries.rist.plainExplanation: Provides Reliable Internet Stream Transport for professional live streaming over unstable networks.
catalog.libraries.rist.technicalExplanat: RIST adds packet recovery, retransmission, timing, and network resilience around media streams. It is designed for contribution and broadcast-style transport.
catalog.libraries.rsvg.plainExplanation: Renders SVG vector graphics into normal image frames. Useful for scalable logos, overlays, and graphic assets.
catalog.libraries.rsvg.technicalExplanat: librsvg interprets SVG paths, shapes, text, gradients, and transforms. Vector graphics can be rasterized cleanly at the target video resolution.
catalog.libraries.rtmp.plainExplanation: Provides RTMP streaming compatibility for older live-streaming servers and workflows.
catalog.libraries.rtmp.technicalExplanat: RTMP carries audio, video, and control messages over a persistent connection. It remains useful for legacy ingest and streaming infrastructure.
catalog.libraries.rubberband.plainExplan: Changes audio speed and pitch with higher-quality time-stretching. Useful for music, dialogue timing, and pitch adjustment.
catalog.libraries.rubberband.technicalEx: Rubber Band analyzes audio timing and spectral content to stretch or shift sound while reducing common artifacts. It is stronger than simple resampling for independent tempo and pitch changes.
catalog.libraries.sdl2.plainExplanation: Provides simple media output and preview support through SDL2. Useful for playback-style testing and display workflows.
catalog.libraries.sdl2.technicalExplanat: SDL2 abstracts windows, audio devices, input, and rendering surfaces. It helps tools present decoded media interactively.
catalog.libraries.shaderc.plainExplanati: Compiles shader programs used by GPU-based video filters. Useful for advanced rendering and GPU processing paths.
catalog.libraries.shaderc.technicalExpla: shaderc compiles GLSL/HLSL-style shader code into SPIR-V. It supports filter pipelines that depend on programmable GPU operations.
catalog.libraries.shine.plainExplanation: Produces MP3 audio using a simple fixed-point encoder. Useful for constrained or compatibility-focused cases.
catalog.libraries.shine.technicalExplana: Shine avoids floating-point-heavy processing and targets simpler MP3 encoding. It is not chosen for maximum MP3 quality, but for predictable lightweight behavior.
catalog.libraries.snappy.plainExplanatio: Provides fast Snappy data compression for formats that use it internally.
catalog.libraries.snappy.technicalExplan: Snappy prioritizes compression and decompression speed over maximum compression ratio. It is useful when container or data formats expect Snappy-compressed blocks.
catalog.libraries.soxr.plainExplanation: Provides high-quality audio sample-rate conversion. Useful when changing audio rates while preserving clarity.
catalog.libraries.soxr.technicalExplanat: SoX Resampler uses precise band-limited resampling algorithms. It reduces aliasing and conversion artifacts better than simpler resamplers.
catalog.libraries.speex.plainExplanation: Handles older Speex speech audio. Useful for legacy voice recordings and communication archives.
catalog.libraries.speex.technicalExplana: Speex is optimized for speech at low to moderate bitrates. It uses voice-focused coding tools rather than general music preservation.
catalog.libraries.srt.plainExplanation: Provides SRT streaming for stable live transport over unreliable networks.
catalog.libraries.srt.technicalExplanati: SRT combines encryption, latency control, packet recovery, and retransmission. It is designed to keep live streams usable despite packet loss or jitter.
catalog.libraries.ssh.plainExplanation: Reads and writes media through SSH and SFTP-style remote access.
catalog.libraries.ssh.technicalExplanati: libssh handles encrypted remote sessions, authentication, and file transfer channels. It allows media workflows to operate directly on secure remote locations.
catalog.libraries.svt-av1.plainExplanati: Produces AV1 video with practical software encoding speed. Commonly chosen for modern compression at usable throughput.
catalog.libraries.svt-av1.technicalExpla: SVT-AV1 uses scalable threading and speed presets to make AV1 encoding more practical on CPUs. It balances compression efficiency against parallel performance.
catalog.libraries.svtjpegxs.plainExplana: Produces JPEG XS video for low-latency professional media workflows.
catalog.libraries.svtjpegxs.technicalExp: JPEG XS is designed for visually lossless, low-delay, low-complexity compression. It targets production transport rather than maximum file-size reduction.
catalog.libraries.tesseract.plainExplana: Reads visible text from images or video frames. Useful for extracting burned-in titles, signs, captions, or document text.
catalog.libraries.tesseract.technicalExp: Tesseract performs optical character recognition by segmenting image regions and recognizing glyph patterns as text. Accuracy depends strongly on image clarity and language data.
catalog.libraries.theora.plainExplanatio: Produces Ogg Theora video for older open-video compatibility.
catalog.libraries.theora.technicalExplan: Theora is an older DCT-based video codec from the Ogg ecosystem. It is mainly relevant for legacy open-format workflows.
catalog.libraries.twolame.plainExplanati: Produces MP2 audio for broadcast, DVD, and older media workflows.
catalog.libraries.twolame.technicalExpla: MP2 uses psychoacoustic audio compression suited to legacy broadcasting and disc standards. TwoLAME provides a mature encoder for that format.
catalog.libraries.vidstab.plainExplanati: Reduces camera shake and makes handheld footage look smoother.
catalog.libraries.vidstab.technicalExpla: vidstab analyzes frame-to-frame motion, estimates unwanted camera movement, and applies compensating transforms. Stabilization may crop or shift the image to hide motion correction edges.
catalog.libraries.vmaf.plainExplanation: Measures perceived video quality by comparing an encoded result with a reference. Useful for evaluating compression choices.
catalog.libraries.vmaf.technicalExplanat: VMAF combines multiple visual quality features into a perceptual score. It is commonly used to compare encoder settings, bitrates, and codec decisions.
catalog.libraries.vo-amrwbenc.plainExpla: Produces AMR-WB wideband speech audio for mobile-style voice compatibility.
catalog.libraries.vo-amrwbenc.technicalE: AMR-WB improves speech bandwidth over narrowband AMR while keeping bitrate low. It is optimized for intelligible voice, not music.
catalog.libraries.vorbis.plainExplanatio: Produces Ogg Vorbis audio with good open-format compatibility. Useful for music and general audio in Ogg workflows.
catalog.libraries.vorbis.technicalExplan: Vorbis uses psychoacoustic modeling and variable bitrate audio compression. It was designed as an open alternative for efficient perceptual audio coding.
catalog.libraries.vvenc.plainExplanation: Produces VVC/H.266 video for very high compression efficiency experiments and next-generation codec testing.
catalog.libraries.vvenc.technicalExplana: VVenc is a software VVC encoder that uses complex partitioning, prediction, transform, in-loop filtering, and rate-distortion decisions. It can compress strongly but usually costs much more CPU time than older codecs.
catalog.libraries.webp.plainExplanation: Reads and writes WebP images used widely on websites. Useful for still images, thumbnails, and image sequences.
catalog.libraries.webp.technicalExplanat: WebP supports lossy and lossless image compression, transparency, and animation. It is designed for compact web image delivery.
catalog.libraries.pocketsphinx.plainExpl: Adds the asr speech-recognition audio filter using CMU PocketSphinx. It cannot currently be built: FFmpeg's asr filter is incompatible with present-day PocketSphinx releases, so selecting it blocks the build.
catalog.libraries.pocketsphinx.technical: PocketSphinx is CMU's lightweight HMM-based speech recognizer, designed for low-resource real-time recognition driven by acoustic and language models. FFmpeg's asr filter feeds decoded audio to it to produce a text transcription of the spoken content. It is blocked by an upstream incompatibility: FFmpeg's af_asr.c still uses the pre-5.0 PocketSphinx API (cmd_ln_t / cmd_ln_parse_r / ps_args, with the old separate sphinxbase). PocketSphinx 5.0 removed that API and merged in sphinxbase, so against current releases (5.1.x) configure's lenient ps_init pkg-config probe passes but the filter fails to compile (FFmpeg trac #10520). Only the legacy 5prealpha sources plus a separately built sphinxbase compile, which is not provided here.
catalog.libraries.whisper.plainExplanati: Converts spoken audio into text using whisper.cpp speech recognition. Useful for transcription and subtitle generation.
catalog.libraries.whisper.technicalExpla: whisper.cpp runs Whisper-style neural speech recognition locally. It analyzes audio features and predicts text segments, often with timestamps suitable for transcript workflows.
catalog.libraries.x264.plainExplanation: Supports H.264 software encoding. A leading H.264/AVC encoder with strong quality, performance, and broad compatibility.
catalog.libraries.x264.technicalExplanat: x264 is a CPU-based H.264 encoder known for software-side decision quality. It uses deep motion search, mode selection, lookahead, adaptive B-frames, adaptive quantization, trellis, and psychovisual rate-distortion choices to balance quality, compression, and speed more flexibly than many fixed hardware encoders.
catalog.libraries.x265.plainExplanation: Supports HEVC/H.265 software encoding for smaller files than H.264 at similar visual quality. Useful when compression efficiency matters more than playback universality.
catalog.libraries.x265.technicalExplanat: x265 uses HEVC’s larger coding units, advanced prediction, in-loop filtering, and rate-distortion analysis. It spends CPU time to reduce bitrate, especially at higher resolutions.
catalog.libraries.xavs.plainExplanation: Encodes video in the AVS1 (Chinese AVS) format. Useful for interoperating with AVS1 broadcast or archival material. This is GPL, so the build moves to a GPL license boundary.
catalog.libraries.xavs.technicalExplanat: libxavs is the reference AVS1 (AVS Part 2 / Jizhun) encoder. It is unrelated to xavs2 (AVS2); select xavs only when you specifically need AVS1 output. FFmpeg requires --enable-gpl for libxavs.
catalog.libraries.xeveb.plainExplanation: Enables MPEG-5 EVC encoding through the EVC base profile, the royalty-free subset of EVC. Uses the same XEVE package as the main xeve row.
catalog.libraries.xeveb.technicalExplana: FFmpeg exposes the EVC base profile as a separate --enable-libxeveb binding next to the main-profile --enable-libxeve. Both link the same XEVE library; the base profile is the patent-free EVC subset intended for unrestricted use.
catalog.libraries.xevdb.plainExplanation: Enables MPEG-5 EVC decoding through the EVC base profile. Uses the same XEVD package as the main xevd row.
catalog.libraries.xevdb.technicalExplana: FFmpeg exposes the EVC base profile as a separate --enable-libxevdb binding next to the main-profile --enable-libxevd. Both link the same XEVD library; the base profile is the patent-free EVC subset.
catalog.libraries.xavs2.plainExplanation: Produces AVS2 video for workflows that need this regional video standard. Useful for compatibility, testing, and specialized distribution.
catalog.libraries.xavs2.technicalExplana: xAVS2 is a software AVS2 encoder. It applies AVS2 prediction, transform, quantization, and entropy coding decisions to create compressed AVS2 video streams.
catalog.libraries.xevd.plainExplanation: Decodes EVC video streams. Useful for reading newer Essential Video Coding material.
catalog.libraries.xevd.technicalExplanat: XEVD reconstructs EVC video from compressed prediction, transform, and entropy-coded data. It is focused on decoding EVC bitstreams into displayable frames.
catalog.libraries.xeve.plainExplanation: Produces EVC video for testing and newer codec workflows.
catalog.libraries.xeve.technicalExplanat: XEVE is a software EVC encoder that applies EVC coding tools through motion estimation, block decisions, transform, quantization, and rate-control logic.
catalog.libraries.xml2.plainExplanation: Reads structured XML data used by some media formats, subtitles, manifests, and metadata workflows.
catalog.libraries.xml2.technicalExplanat: libxml2 parses XML documents, elements, attributes, namespaces, and structured text. It is useful when media features depend on XML-based metadata or descriptions.
catalog.libraries.xvid.plainExplanation: Produces older MPEG-4 Part 2 video for legacy players and devices.
catalog.libraries.xvid.technicalExplanat: Xvid encodes the older ASP-style MPEG-4 video format using motion prediction, DCT transforms, quantization, and rate control. It is mainly useful for compatibility with old playback ecosystems.
catalog.libraries.zimg.plainExplanation: Improves image resizing, pixel-format conversion, and color handling. Useful for clean scaling and careful video conversion.
catalog.libraries.zimg.technicalExplanat: zimg focuses on high-quality resampling, colorspace conversion, dithering, and bit-depth handling. It is often preferred when image conversion quality matters.
catalog.libraries.zmq.plainExplanation: Enables message-based runtime control for supported processing workflows. Useful for automation and interactive control.
catalog.libraries.zmq.technicalExplanati: ZeroMQ provides lightweight messaging patterns between processes. In media workflows, it can send control commands or parameter changes while processing is running.
catalog.libraries.zvbi.plainExplanation: Extracts teletext and VBI data from older broadcast sources. Useful for hidden captions, pages, and broadcast text information.
catalog.libraries.zvbi.technicalExplanat: VBI data is carried outside the visible picture area in analog-style broadcast signals. libzvbi decodes teletext pages, subtitles, and related broadcast text services.
catalog.options.default-ffmpeg.plainExpl: Builds the main command-line converter most users run.
catalog.options.default-ffmpeg.technical: Checked because ffmpeg.exe is part of a normal program build.
catalog.options.default-ffprobe.plainExp: Builds the media inspection tool used to read stream and container information.
catalog.options.default-ffprobe.technica: Checked because ffprobe.exe is part of a normal program build.
catalog.options.default-programs.plainEx: FFmpeg normally builds command-line programs such as ffmpeg.exe and ffprobe.exe.
catalog.options.default-programs.technic: Checked because programs are built in a normal source build. Disable only if you want libraries without command-line tools.
catalog.options.default-static.plainExpl: FFmpeg normally builds static libraries from source.
catalog.options.default-static.technical: Checked because this is normal FFmpeg configure behavior. No extra flag is needed unless you choose a different output type.
catalog.options.disable-asm.plainExplana:
Uses slower but simpler C code paths if assembly causes build problems.
**<red>Risk</red>: this removes nearly all SIMD optimization, so encoding and decoding can be several times slower. Use it only when assembly actually breaks the build.**
catalog.options.disable-asm.technicalNot: Normally leave unchecked because FFmpeg is faster with assembly optimizations.
catalog.options.disable-autodetect.displ: Do not auto-use hidden system libraries
catalog.options.disable-autodetect.plain: Makes the build less surprising by using only explicitly selected external libraries.
catalog.options.disable-autodetect.techn: Good for transparent/reproducible builds. Select this when you want the Review page to explain every external dependency.
catalog.options.disable-debug.plainExpla: Makes normal-use output smaller and simpler.
catalog.options.disable-debug.technicalN: Not a normal source default. Select this for ordinary release-style local builds; leave unchecked when investigating build or runtime problems.
catalog.options.disable-doc.plainExplana: Makes the build smaller by not building local documentation files.
catalog.options.disable-doc.technicalNot: Not a normal source default. Select this when you only need binaries/libraries and do not need generated docs.
catalog.options.disable-ffplay.plainExpl: Skips the simple playback test program.
catalog.options.disable-ffplay.technical: Useful when SDL playback support is unnecessary. ffmpeg.exe and ffprobe.exe are unaffected.
catalog.options.disable-stripping.plainE: Keeps more build information for debugging.
catalog.options.disable-stripping.techni: Usually unnecessary for ordinary users, but useful when diagnosing crashes or build problems.
catalog.options.disable-x86asm.plainExpl: Try this when NASM/YASM-related build problems occur.
catalog.options.enable-shared.plainExpla:
Creates DLL-style FFmpeg libraries for other programs to load.
**<red>Risk</red>: this switches the output to DLLs and turns off static builds, which often breaks linking against the static external libraries this tool installs — the build can fail, or produce an ffmpeg.exe that needs extra DLLs at run time.**
catalog.options.enable-shared.technicalN: FFmpeg platform documentation describes --enable-shared as the way to build FFmpeg libraries as DLLs on Windows. This changes the output type, so it is not selected by default here.
catalog.options.enable-small.plainExplan: Asks FFmpeg to prefer smaller output files over speed.
catalog.options.enable-small.technicalNo: Useful for constrained environments; may reduce performance.
catalog.options.enable-lto.plainExplanat: Lets the compiler optimize across files for a smaller and sometimes faster binary.
catalog.options.enable-lto.technicalNote: Increases build time and memory use. Leave unchecked if linking fails or runs out of memory.
catalog.options.enable-runtime-cpudetect: Detect CPU features at run time
Builds one binary that picks CPU optimizations while running, so it works across different processors.
Useful when sharing the build with other machines. Slightly slower than a build tuned for one specific CPU.
catalog.options.pkg-config-static.plainE: Tells pkg-config to pull the full static dependency chain when linking external libraries.
catalog.options.pkg-config-static.techni: Often required for static Windows builds that use external libraries, so configure can find every transitive dependency. Has no effect on a shared/DLL build.
catalog.options.disable-network.plainExp: Builds FFmpeg without any network protocols for a smaller, offline-only tool.

catalog.libraries.cairo.plainExplanation: Provides 2D vector drawing support for generated graphics, overlays, and filter visuals. Useful when media processing needs drawn shapes or rendered graphic elements.
catalog.libraries.cairo.technicalExplana: Cairo renders vector primitives such as paths, text, strokes, fills, and surfaces. In media workflows, it is mainly valuable for producing clean graphics that are composited into frames.
catalog.libraries.glslang.plainExplanati: Compiles GLSL shader code for GPU-based video processing. Useful for advanced graphics and compute-style filter paths.
catalog.libraries.glslang.technicalExpla: glslang translates shader source into intermediate forms used by GPU APIs. It matters when filters rely on programmable shader stages rather than fixed CPU processing.
catalog.libraries.cuda-nvcc.plainExplana: Compiles FFmpeg's CUDA-accelerated filters with NVIDIA's nvcc compiler. nvcc ships only in the proprietary CUDA Toolkit, which is not available as an MSYS2 package.
catalog.libraries.cuda-nvcc.technicalExp: nvcc compiles FFmpeg's CUDA filter kernels (e.g. scale_cuda, thumbnail_cuda, yadif_cuda) into GPU device code so those filters run on the NVIDIA GPU instead of the CPU. It targets a specific CUDA and driver version, so the compiled kernels must match the compute capability the GPU supports.
catalog.libraries.opencv.plainExplanatio: Provides computer-vision processing for image analysis and experimental visual filters.
catalog.libraries.opencv.technicalExplan: OpenCV contains algorithms for detection, tracking, feature extraction, filtering, and image transformations. It is useful when video frames need machine-vision style analysis.
catalog.libraries.opencolorio.plainExpla: Applies studio-grade color management for film, animation, and post-production workflows.
catalog.libraries.opencolorio.technicalE: OpenColorIO manages color spaces, looks, transforms, and production color pipelines. It is built for controlled color movement across cameras, displays, and grading systems.
catalog.libraries.dvdread.plainExplanati: Reads DVD media structures for extraction, inspection, or conversion. Useful when the source is a DVD folder or disc layout.
catalog.libraries.dvdread.technicalExpla: libdvdread accesses DVD-Video files, IFO metadata, and VOB streams. It provides lower-level DVD reading that navigation-aware tools can build on.
catalog.libraries.kvazaar.plainExplanati: Provides HEVC/H.265 software encoding with an open research-oriented encoder. Useful when HEVC output is needed through a non-x265 path.
catalog.libraries.kvazaar.technicalExpla: Kvazaar is a CPU HEVC encoder developed around modular coding tools and parallel processing research. It focuses on standards-compliant HEVC compression with controllable analysis depth.
catalog.libraries.dvdnav.plainExplanatio: Reads DVD-Video navigation structures such as menus, titles, chapters, and program chains. Useful for disc-style DVD workflows.
catalog.libraries.dvdnav.technicalExplan: DVD-Video is not just a video file; it contains navigation commands, cells, titles, and menu logic. libdvdnav interprets that structure so the correct playback path can be followed.
catalog.libraries.mbedtls.plainExplanati: Provides lightweight TLS support for encrypted network media access. Useful when a smaller security backend is preferred.
catalog.libraries.mbedtls.technicalExpla: mbedTLS implements TLS, cryptographic primitives, certificates, and secure socket behavior with a compact design often used in embedded and minimal environments.
catalog.libraries.onnxruntime.plainExpla: Runs supported deep-learning filters through ONNX Runtime. Useful for model-based analysis or enhancement workflows.
catalog.libraries.onnxruntime.technicalE: ONNX Runtime executes neural-network graphs stored in the ONNX format. It provides an inference engine for filters that use trained models.
catalog.libraries.vapoursynth.plainExpla: Opens VapourSynth script-based video processing chains. Useful when advanced scripted filtering must feed frames into a media workflow.
catalog.libraries.vapoursynth.technicalE: VapourSynth is a frame server with Python-driven filter graphs. It generates processed frames on demand, often for restoration, resizing, denoising, or complex scripted preprocessing.
catalog.libraries.jack.plainExplanation: Connects to JACK audio routing for studio-style capture and playback workflows. Useful in professional Linux audio environments.
catalog.libraries.jack.technicalExplanat: JACK provides low-latency routing between audio applications. It is used when media processing must interact with a live audio graph rather than ordinary device capture.
catalog.libraries.pulse.plainExplanation: Connects to PulseAudio for Linux desktop audio capture or playback workflows.
catalog.libraries.pulse.technicalExplana: PulseAudio manages application audio streams, devices, mixing, and routing. It is relevant when media processing must interact with the desktop audio server.
catalog.libraries.rabbitmq.plainExplanat: Connects media workflows to RabbitMQ message queues. Useful for automated processing systems.
catalog.libraries.rabbitmq.technicalExpl: RabbitMQ-C communicates with AMQP brokers. It helps media tools send or receive structured messages as part of distributed pipelines.

catalog.libraries.avisynthplus.plainExpl: Opens AviSynth script-based video processing chains directly. Useful when a workflow already depends on AviSynth filters or scripted frame processing.
catalog.libraries.avisynthplus.technical: AviSynth works as a frame server: scripts generate processed video frames on demand. This allows filtering, restoration, resizing, and source chaining to happen before the frames enter the media pipeline.
catalog.libraries.davs2.plainExplanation: Decodes AVS2 video streams. Useful for regional, broadcast, or compatibility workflows involving AVS2 material.
catalog.libraries.davs2.technicalExplana: libdavs2 implements AVS2 bitstream decoding, reconstructing frames from AVS2 prediction, transform, and entropy-coded data. It is mainly relevant when AVS2 sources need to be read reliably.
catalog.libraries.uavs3d.plainExplanatio: Decodes AVS3 video streams. Useful for AVS3 test material, regional standards, and compatibility workflows.
catalog.libraries.uavs3d.technicalExplan: libuavs3d reconstructs AVS3 frames from compressed prediction, transform, and entropy-coded data. It is focused on reading AVS3 rather than general video enhancement.
catalog.libraries.lcevc-dec.plainExplana: Decodes LCEVC enhancement layers that improve a base video stream. Useful when content uses layered video enhancement.
catalog.libraries.lcevc-dec.technicalExp: LCEVC carries extra correction data over a lower-resolution or simpler base stream. The decoder reconstructs improved detail by combining the base video with the enhancement layer.
catalog.libraries.mpeghdec.plainExplanat: Decodes MPEG-H 3D Audio for immersive and object-based audio content.
catalog.libraries.mpeghdec.technicalExpl: MPEG-H can carry channels, objects, scene information, and personalization metadata. The decoder reconstructs the intended immersive audio presentation.
catalog.libraries.openvino.plainExplanat: Runs supported AI inference filters with Intel-oriented acceleration. Useful for model-based video or image processing.
catalog.libraries.openvino.technicalExpl: OpenVINO optimizes neural-network inference for Intel CPUs, integrated GPUs, and related accelerators. It focuses on efficient deployment of trained models.
catalog.libraries.tensorflow.plainExplan: Runs supported deep-learning filters through the TensorFlow C API. Useful for model-based image or video analysis.
catalog.libraries.tensorflow.technicalEx: TensorFlow executes trained neural-network graphs. In media processing, it can drive inference filters that classify, enhance, detect, or transform visual content.
catalog.libraries.torch.plainExplanation: Runs supported deep-learning filters through Torch-based model execution. Useful for PyTorch-style inference workflows.
catalog.libraries.torch.technicalExplana: libtorch provides C++ execution for TorchScript and related model workflows. It allows trained neural networks to be used inside media processing pipelines.
catalog.libraries.quirc.plainExplanation: Decodes QR codes from video frames or images. Useful for automation, scanning, and visual metadata workflows.
catalog.libraries.quirc.technicalExplana: quirc locates QR patterns, corrects perspective, applies error correction, and extracts the encoded payload from image data.
catalog.libraries.klvanc.plainExplanatio: Processes vertical ancillary data used in broadcast video. Useful for metadata carried alongside video lines.
catalog.libraries.klvanc.technicalExplan: VANC can contain captions, timecode, AFD, SCTE data, and other broadcast metadata. libklvanc parses and manages that non-picture information.
catalog.libraries.smbclient.plainExplana: Reads from and writes to SMB/CIFS network shares. Useful for media stored on Windows-style network folders. It cannot be built on Windows yet, so it is listed last in this section and stays unavailable until a Windows version of libsmbclient exists.
catalog.libraries.smbclient.technicalExp: libsmbclient speaks the SMB protocol, handling authentication, paths, file access, and network share communication. It is part of Samba, which has no MSYS2 package and no prebuilt mingw-w64 build and does not compile natively on Windows (it needs a POSIX environment).
catalog.libraries.libtls.plainExplanatio: Provides TLS-encrypted network communication through a compact TLS interface. Useful for secure network media access.
catalog.libraries.libtls.technicalExplan: libtls exposes a simpler TLS API over LibreSSL-style secure transport. It handles encrypted sessions, certificates, and protected data exchange.

libraries.presets.ai.name: AI
libraries.presets.ai.plain: Model-focused set for inference, transcription, OCR, vision, and quality analysis.
libraries.presets.ai.technical: (As of FFmpeg 8.1.2) Hidden preset: Default plus AI-focused additions only. It adds inference backends, transcription, OCR, computer vision, GPU processing, and image workflow libraries without inheriting Efficiency, Compatibility, Editor, or Full.
libraries.presets.streaming.name: Streaming
libraries.presets.streaming.plain: Live-streaming set for hardware encoding, protocols, audio, scaling, and GPU processing.
libraries.presets.streaming.technical: (As of FFmpeg 8.1.2) Hidden preset: Default plus streaming-focused additions only. It adds high-quality live audio handling, RTMP/RIST transport, TLS support, and GPU-oriented processing without inheriting Efficiency, Compatibility, Editor, or Full.
libraries.presets.maxtest.name: Dev: Maximum test
libraries.presets.maxtest.plain: Developer preset: every catalog library except unimplemented ones and conflicting alternatives.
libraries.presets.maxtest.technical: (As of FFmpeg 8.1.2) Developer-only preset, visible after the hidden About-tab unlock. Selects every library in the catalog except those with no implemented build recipe and the losing side of each mutually-exclusive group (one TLS backend, shaderc over glslang). Libraries unavailable for the active profile are dropped. Intended only to exercise the widest buildable configuration during development.
